text:
devon: Heads-up — we're doing a GPU node-pool scale-down in us-east-1 at 17:00. Several long-running training jobs still running. PDBs exist but cluster-autoscaler is getting blocked. Need quick runbook for safe drains that won't kill jobs or stall capacity for hours.

alex: +1. Quick notes: CA won't evict pods that are not safe-to-evict. We use the annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true/false` on pods. Also PDBs can prevent scale-down if removing a node would violate minAvailable.

maria: For batch jobs we should prefer a low-priorityClass so they can be preempted. But training jobs that checkpoint mid-epoch need graceful shutdown. Suggest a "drain leash" process: cordon -> send SIGTERM via preStop that triggers checkpoint -> wait X mins -> drain.

john: Agree. We already have `preStop` hooks for the tuners, but not for large TF jobs. Small checklist: 1) add `safe-to-evict` annotation where safe; 2) ensure job controllers have `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` >= 300; 3) create a one-time cordon+annotate workflow to give apps warmup time.

kevin: CA logs earlier showed: `ScaleDown: candidate node node-pool-gpu-7 blocked by PDB: job-xyz (minAvailable)` — so PDBs are the blocker, not kubelet evictions. We should either temporarily relax PDBs for batch or drain nodes manually after app checkpoint.

devon: Is there a way to mark certain pods as "drain-wait" so CA skips them until our runbook runs? I don't want CA to flip flop.

sre-bot: autoscaler: scaleDownCandidates=[node-pool-gpu-7], blockedBy=[PodDisruptionBudget(job-xyz,minAvailable=1,available=1)]

alex: You can set `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` to tell CA NOT to evict. But that's the opposite of what you want. For temporary suppression of CA decisions, we sometimes set a node annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: true` to prevent scale-down of that node until we clear it.

maria: Another pattern: put long-running training jobs into a separate nodePool with `maxSurge=0` and `scaleDownDelay` config. But that's heavier. For today I'd do: cordon the node, run a `kubectl exec` to trigger checkpoint, wait, then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=15m <node>` and uncordon if something fails.

john: Example drain command we use:
```
kubectl cordon <node>
# trigger app checkpoint (custom script)
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=300 --timeout=15m
```
Note: `--force` needed if local pods are blocking. Use carefully.

kevin: We should avoid `--force` unless we've validated checkpointing. If a job doesn't exit gracefully and we force, we lose progress. For the runbook, add a health-check poll that watches for pods to enter Terminating and confirms they saved state (look for `checkpoint-uploaded` annotation/event).

devon: Good point. I'll add the quick checkpoint trigger to the job templates and run the manual cordon/drain for the 3 nodes with active jobs. Can someone run through one with me?

alex: I can join. Also proposing a short-term change: add a `drain-warmup=true` label to nodes we plan to scale down; an operator script will look for that label and extend `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` for pods on that node via patching the pod spec (yes it's ugly) or send a checkpoint hook.

maria: Longer term: add a `gpu-batch` priorityClass with `preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority` and a CA filter that prefers evicting those. Also consider taint+dedicated pool for critical infra so CA won't touch them.

devon: Action items: 1) manual cordon+checkpoint+drain for 3 nodes today (I'll run) 2) alex to make a tiny script to label nodes `drain-warmup=true` and an operator that waits 5m after label before uncordoning 3) maria/john to draft policy for priorityClass + taint approach next week.

kevin: I'll update the runbook in Confluence with the `kubectl` commands and the checklist for verifying checkpoint events. Also add example Pod annotation snippet: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"  # for stateless helper pods
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 600
  lifecycle:
    preStop:
      exec:
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/checkpoint || true"]
```

devon: Thanks all — ping me in #eng-sre when someone's ready to pair on the first node. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: started runbook: `gpu-scale-down-drain` (runbook-id: rb-2026-03-18-01)
